title: Impossible Lab
summary: A first-person puzzle laboratory where the rooms refuse to behave.

detail.Idea: A laboratory where each world has a different rule, and discoveries can be combined across worlds.
detail.Work: A first-person browser game with four experiments, a journal, local saves and an ending. The creatures use original procedural geometry and articulated rigs in Three.js; the interface uses React.
detail.Try: Collect the four cores, combine three discoveries at the workbench, and bring them to the reactor.
detail.Development: Folio gained a readable chambered shell and moving sensory fans. Captain Liability now physically opens during the valid pulse window. Aurelia's bells react to tuning. Camera bounds, collision and field-note typography were refined together.
detail.Takeaway: The creature's pose, the attack effect and the valid player action need to follow the same clock. A convincing tell must also be mechanically true.

comparison.caption: The same room and camera: a lower silhouette reveals the chambered shell and sensory fans. Larger field labels make the objective easier to read.

title: Theory Studio
summary: A music workspace for harmony, counterpoint, figured bass, and the details between the notes.

detail.Idea: Make the relationships between notes visible while working through harmony and counterpoint.
detail.Work: A music workspace with score notation, figured-bass realization, candidate comparisons and individual rule checks.
detail.Try: Open a built-in figured-bass exercise, review its pitches, then realize and check the voices.
detail.Development: The public browser edition keeps the usable theory and manual-transcription workflow. Automatic recognition and MusicXML import belong to the desktop edition and are identified in the interface.
detail.Takeaway: A useful music tool needs to explain individual checks and preserve review decisions, rather than presenting an unexplained pass or fail.

title: NeighborReady

detail.Work: A bilingual student app with household planning, practice exercises and an offline copy.
detail.Try: Use sample household information, build a plan and explore the practice workflow.
detail.Development: The public exhibit includes the usable app and its offline behavior; 48 tests cover the implemented planning and state logic.
detail.Context: A student preparation prototype, not live emergency alerts or a certified safety assessment.

title: Off the Page

detail.Idea: Explore musical improvisation as a living practice with a history, rather than an exception to the score.
detail.Work: A scroll-driven music-history website with an editorial layout and GSAP motion.
detail.Try: Follow the chronology and its musical examples from the earlier traditions to the present.
detail.Development: The site is packaged as a standalone exhibit with asset paths that work beneath the portfolio's project directory.

title: Axiom
summary: A flyable chalkboard universe of mathematics, with connected topics and an SAT practice mode.

detail.Idea: Make mathematics feel like a connected place to explore, with practice available beside the ideas.
detail.Work: A flyable chalkboard graph containing 335 topics, 69 mathematicians, 574 prerequisite links and 670 starter problems, plus a 28-skill SAT practice space.
detail.Try: Follow a prerequisite path, open a topic or mathematician, use the timeline, or practice a SAT skill.
detail.Development: A retained scene and bounded drawing caches replace repeated chalk rasterization. Animated glows and paths remain live; the mobile practice map scrolls at a readable scale.
detail.Takeaway: Fast JavaScript alone does not guarantee smooth drawing. Reducing repeated GPU submissions fixed the pan-and-zoom bottleneck.
